value="<b>Partition P0 — LEADER<br></b><p>A partition can become <strong>huge</strong>.&nbsp;<span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Instead of keeping one gigantic file, Kafka breaks it into smaller files called </span><strong style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">segments</strong><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">:<br></span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">append-only, split into segments:<br></span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">[seg 0 closed] [seg 1 closed] [seg 2 ACTIVE]<br></span><b style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">offset</b><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));"> = a message's position in the log<br></span><i style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">sequential writes;<br></i><span style="font-style: italic; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Segment 0:<br></span><span style="font-style: italic; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">offset 0 ─────── 999</span></p><i><div><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Segment 1:</span></div><div>offset 1000 ──── 1999</div><div><br></div><div>Segment 2:</div><div>offset 2000 ──── 2999&nbsp; ← currently writing</div></i>" vertex="1"> value="<b>Leader state</b><br>ISR = in-sync replicas, Replicas that are <strong>up-to-date with the leader</strong>.<br><br>LEO per replica -&nbsp;<span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Log End Offset</span><p><strong>LEO = next position where a new message can be written.</strong></p>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="230" width="140" x="955" y="175" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-18" parent="1" value="<b>Serve</b><br><p>When a consumer asks for a message, Kafka wants to send it <strong>as fast as possible</strong>.</p><p><strong>OS Page Cache</strong><br>→ Recently used Kafka data stays in <strong>RAM</strong>, so Kafka doesn't need to read disk every time.</p><p><strong>Zero-copy / sendfile</strong><br>→ Kafka can send data <strong>directly from the OS cache/file to the network</strong>, without unnecessarily copying the data through Kafka's application memory.</p>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="265" width="155" x="1110" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Monitoring</b> — under-replicated partitions · ISR shrink rate · consumer lag · request latency · disk usage. Alert BEFORE data is at risk." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="70" width="990" x="900" y="1040" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-56" edge="1" parent="1" source="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-27" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;html=1;endArrow=block;endFill=1;strokeWidth=2;strokeColor=#d79b00;fontSize=11;fontColor=#d79b00;labelBackgroundColor=#ffffff;dashed=1;fontSize=15;fontStyle=1;exitX=0.53;exitY=1;entryX=0.15;entryY=0;" target="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-51" value="⑨ closed segments age out"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-57" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=16;fontColor=#222222;fontStyle=1;spacing=4;" value="How to read it — follow the numbers" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="900" x="40" y="1170" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-58" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Write path (①–⑥)</b><br>① Producer picks a partition: hash(key) % N, then batches<br>② The batch goes to that partition's LEADER (found via metadata).<br>③ Leader appends to the active segment, assigns offsets, drops duplicates (producer_id + seq).<br>④ Followers PULL the new data and append it to their own copies.<br>⑤ When every in-sync replica has it, the HIGH WATERMARK moves forward = committed.<br>⑥ Leader acks the producer (with acks=all).<br><br><b>Why pull-based replication + ISR?</b> The leader never waits on a slow follower: it just drops it from the ISR. Durability = "all CURRENT ISR members have it"." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="370" width="610" x="40" y="1210" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-59" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Read path &amp; control (⑦–⑨, C1–C3)</b><br>⑦ Consumers fetch from the leader (long-poll), only up to the high watermark, via zero-copy.<br>⑧ After processing, they commit their offset to __consumer_offsets.<br>⑨ Retention / compaction / tiering work on old closed segments in the background.<br>C1–C3 Admin changes → controller (Raft) → pushed to brokers; clients ask the controller who leads which partition.<br><br><b>If a leader dies:</b> the controller elects a new leader from the ISR → no committed message is lost. Clients refresh metadata and continue.<br><br><b>Trade-offs to say out loud:</b> acks=all = safer but slower · more partitions = more parallelism but more metadata and slower recovery · order only per partition." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="370" width="610" x="670" y="1210" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="ZyXYzHzgOWnOrjyoNF_w-60" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Build it in this order</b><br>1. Single-node log: append-only segments + sparse index (offset → file position)<br>2. Network server: produce &amp; fetch APIs, batching, page cache<br>3. Partitions: hash(key) → many logs, spread across brokers<br>4. Replication: leader/follower, pull fetch, ISR, high watermark, leader epochs<br>5. Consumer groups: coordinator, rebalance, offsets topic<br>6. Controller: metadata in Raft, leader election, broker registry<br>7. Retention, then compaction, then tiered storage<br>8. Idempotent producer, then transactions (exactly-once)<br><br><b>Each stage is usable on its own</b> — and each exists because of one earlier decision: <i>append-only log → partitions → replicas → groups → controller.</i>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="370" width="630" x="1300" y="1210" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.p:
A partition can become huge. Instead of keeping one gigantic file, Kafka breaks it into smaller files called segments:
append-only, split into segments:
[seg 0 closed] [seg 1 closed] [seg 2 ACTIVE]
offset = a message's position in the log
sequential writes;
Segment 0:
offset 0 ─────── 999

div.div:
Leader state
ISR = in-sync replicas, Replicas that are up-to-date with the leader.
LEO per replica - Log End Offset
LEO = next position where a new message can be written.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 137px; height: 1px; padding-top: 261px; margin-left: 1183px;

div.p: When a consumer asks for a message, Kafka wants to send it as fast as possible.

OS Page Cache
→ Recently used Kafka data stays in RAM, so Kafka doesn't need to read disk every time.

Zero-copy / sendfile
→ Kafka can send data directly from the OS cache/file to the network, without unnecessarily copying the data through Kafka's application memory.

div.div: How to read it — follow the numbers

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 592px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1383px; margin-left: 114px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Write path (①–⑥)
① Producer picks a partition: hash(key) % N, then batches
② The batch goes to that partition's LEADER (found via metadata).
③ Leader appends to the active segment, assigns offsets, drops duplicates (producer_id + seq).
④ Followers PULL the new data and append it to their own copies.
⑤ When every in-sync replica has it, the HIGH WATERMARK moves forward = committed.
⑥ Leader acks the producer (with acks=all).
Why pull-based replication + ISR? The leader never waits on a slow follower: it just drops it from the ISR. Durability = "all CURRENT ISR members have it".

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 592px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1383px; margin-left: 744px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Read path & control (⑦–⑨, C1–C3)
⑦ Consumers fetch from the leader (long-poll), only up to the high watermark, via zero-copy.
⑧ After processing, they commit their offset to __consumer_offsets.
⑨ Retention / compaction / tiering work on old closed segments in the background.
C1–C3 Admin changes → controller (Raft) → pushed to brokers; clients ask the controller who leads which partition.
If a leader dies: the controller elects a new leader from the ISR → no committed message is lost. Clients refresh metadata and continue.
Trade-offs to say out loud: acks=all = safer but slower · more partitions = more parallelism but more metadata and slower recovery · order only per partition.

div.div:
Build it in this order
1. Single-node log: append-only segments + sparse index (offset → file position)
2. Network server: produce & fetch APIs, batching, page cache
3. Partitions: hash(key) → many logs, spread across brokers
4. Replication: leader/follower, pull fetch, ISR, high watermark, leader epochs
5. Consumer groups: coordinator, rebalance, offsets topic
6. Controller: metadata in Raft, leader election, broker registry
7. Retention, then compaction, then tiered storage
8. Idempotent producer, then transactions (exactly-once)
Each stage is usable on its own — and each exists because of one earlier decision: append-only log → partitions → replicas → groups → controller.
